text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Liverpool and Fulham at Anfield.
The hosts have their sights firmly set on a first Premier League title since the 2019-20 campaign after a superb start, one that has them heading into this game in third.

They will move to within two points of leaders Arsenal with a win here, and they will fancy their chances considering their impressive home record of late, winning all 10 of their games at Anfield in all competitions this season.
The visitors picked up a much-needed win at home to Wolves on Monday, their first victory in five Premier League games.
However, positive results for Everton and Burnley on Saturday mean Fulham could do with another win here to extend the gap to the relegation zone to 11 points.
Jurgen Klopp makes six changes from the 4-0 thumping of LASK in midweek that secured Liverpool's place in the Europa League knockout stages, with three of those coming in his backline.
Matip, Van Dijk and Alexander-Arnold come in for Quansah, Konate and Gomez, while Szoboszlai and Mac Allister return for Endo and Elliott.
Nunez is preferred to Gakpo up top, despite the Dutchman netting twice in the LASK win.
Marco Silva makes three alterations to his starting XI from the Wolves victory, with a couple of those changes perhaps surprising given their performances in that game.
Cairney and Willian both impressed, the latter scoring twice from the spot, yet they drop to the bench for Palhinha and Wilson.
The other change sees Tete come in for Castagne at right-back.
The two sets of players make their way into the cauldron of noise that is Anfield, and we are now just moments away from kick-off.
The visitors kick us off and we are under way on Merseyside!
The first chance of the game falls to Diaz as a clever spin takes him away from Bassey, though his eventual shot is at a nice height for Leno, who makes a comfortable save.
Liverpool have lost just one of their last 10 Premier League games against Fulham (seven wins, two draws), a 1-0 home loss in March 2021.
Fulham are making sure to get bodies behind the ball when Liverpool have possession, and this could prove a frustrating outing for the hosts if they just go through the motions.
NO GOAL! Fulham hearts are temporarily in mouths as Leno spills Szoboszlai's shot straight into the path of Diaz.
The Colombia international manages to nudge the ball past the goalkeeper before Salah turns home, but the flag immediately goes up for offside to curtail the celebrations.
There is a VAR check, though that confirms the on-field decision and it remains 0-0!
Leno is down and seemingly in a lot of pain after that incident that led to the disallowed goal.
Silva may be forced into an early change between the sticks.
Leno is still down receiving treatment, and it seems the former Arsenal man has a problem with his head after that coming-together with Diaz.
Rodak is on the touchline warming up.
Despite the lengthy treatment, Leno is going to try and play on here with a bandage around his head.
Liverpool will be looking to test him as quickly as they can.
The delay for Leno to be treated has taken the momentum out of the game, with both teams struggling to get back into their full attacking flow since the restart.
Szoboszlai is brought down around 30 yards out from goal, and the likes of Alexander-Arnold and Salah will be fancying their chances of hitting the target from here.
GOOOAAALLL!!!! LIVERPOOL LEAD THROUGH AN OWN GOAL!!! Alexander-Arnold has so much quality with that wand of a right foot, and he uses every bit of it on this stunning free-kick.
He arrows it over the wall before the ball kisses the underside of the crossbar and goes in off Leno's back, putting Liverpool 1-0 up at Anfield!
It is absolutely vital for the visitors that they do not concede another goal in the next couple of minutes, or this could end up being a really long outing.
Liverpool are knocking the ball out superbly and look full of confidence now.
GOOOAAALLL!!!! WILSON LEVELS!!! That lead didn't last very long! Iwobi slips a nice pass into the path of Robinson, who fires a low first-time cross into the danger area.
Wilson is there to turn home, poking through the legs of Kelleher to score against his former club and make it 1-1!
Robinson's delivery was drilled in, and Wilson just had to get the slightest of touches on it to divert into the back of the net.
That goal came from out of nowhere really, with Fulham yet to trouble Liverpool at all until equalising.
That should give the visitors hope they can come away with a shock result here.
Tsimikas whips a free-kick delivery into the Fulham box, but Matip cannot find the target with his header and it bounces away harmlessly for a goal-kick.
Liverpool have now scored in their last 24 Premier League games.
They rarely fail to find the back of the net.
Robinson strides forward from left-back before letting fly, though his shot takes a deflection off Matip and goes behind for a corner.
Silva will be encouraged by how his team have grown into this contest.
A corner causes havoc in the Fulham box, sitting up nicely for Van Dijk to lash goalwards.
However, Wilson does brilliantly to race out to the Liverpool man and block his fierce effort before the visitors eventually scramble away.
Fulham have scored just four goals in 16 Premier League away games against Liverpool, and never more than once in a match.
It's the lowest goals-per-game ratio (0.25) of any team to play more than 10 away games against an opponent in the competition, though they have already bettered that here.
GOOOAAALLL!!!! MAC ALLISTER SCORES A STUNNER!!! A loose Jimenez header needlessly gives away possession, and Mac Allister looks to catch out Leno by shooting early.
He does exactly that, and from all of 30 yards out, the ball finds its way into the top corner as Mac Allister puts the hosts 2-1 ahead with another brilliant goal!
Fulham will be relatively pleased with their defensive efforts, yet they find themselves behind because of two exquisite goals.
That is the problem you face sometimes when going up against a side with Liverpool's quality.
As we close in on half-time, Silva will be desperate for his side to make it to the interval just the one goal behind.
They have acquitted themselves well so far, though that could change if Liverpool find another goal before the break.
There will be nine minutes of additional time at the end of this first half, in large part due to the lengthy break for Leno to receive treatment early on.
GOOOAAALLL!!! TETE MAKES IT 2-2!!! A corner from the left comes in, and Jimenez manages to flick it on to Tete behind him.
The right-back improvises by swinging his right boot at it, and Kelleher cannot keep the ball out as it goes into the back of the net.
The flag initially goes up for offside, but after a lengthy VAR check, the decision is reversed and Fulham can celebrate as they level on the stroke of half-time!
Silva's men are looking eager to try and get their noses in front for the first time in this game.
They are the side pressing now.
NO GOAL!!! Liverpool again fail to deal with a corner as Palhinha rises highest to nod Pereira's delivery goalwards.
Kelleher gets down to his right to make the save, but he pushes the ball straight into the path of the incoming Ream, who prods into the back of the net.
However, the flag again goes up for offside, and this time the decision stands as it remains 2-2!

Since a 1-0 defeat to Fulham at Anfield in March 2021, which was the sixth consecutive league defeat suffered by the Reds on home soil, Liverpool have lost just one of their last 48 Premier League matches at Anfield (37 wins, 10 draws) – a 2-1 loss to Leeds United in October 2022.
Salah can score his 200th Liverpool goal in this game, and he tests Leno with a low shot.
The angle was always against him, and the Fulham goalkeeper is able to make the save.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-2 FULHAM
The half-time whistle blows to bring a pulsating first half to an end with the scoreline 2-2 at Anfield.

Liverpool have twice led through stunning goals, the first of which came from Alexander-Arnold with 20 minutes gone, arrowing a superb free-kick in off the bar and then Leno to hand the hosts the lead.
They would be pegged back just four minutes later, Robinson firing in a low cross which was turned home by Wilson against his former club.
Liverpool would regain the lead through Mac Allister, who struck from all of 30 yards out with an incredible finish.
However, the visitors would again level before the break, Jimenez nodding the ball on to Tete, who poked past Kelleher and in to send the teams back to the changing rooms at two apiece.
Silva will be encouraged by his team's performance in that half.

So many teams go a goal down at Anfield and crumble, but Silva's men are made of stronger stuff and could even have gone into the break ahead, had Ream's disallowed goal stood moments before half-time.
For Klopp, Arsenal's win on Saturday means three points is imperative here, and he will be looking for his players to ramp up the pressure following half-time.
The hosts get the ball rolling again for the second half.

This is the the first time Liverpool have both scored and conceded two or more goals in the first half of a Premier League game at Anfield since September 2020 against Leeds, and the first time Fulham did so home or away in the division since October 2018 at Cardiff.
Both sides have picked up where they left off in the first half, throwing plenty of bodies forward in their pursuit of the fifth goal in this game.
Szoboszlai fires goalwards from 25 yards out, but his dipping shot ends up flying well wide of the left post.
He will be disappointed with that effort.
OFF THE BAR!!! Liverpool fly forward on the counter-attack, and Salah slides a throughball into the path of Nunez in the Fulham box.
The Uruguay international races onto it before letting fly, but the ball cannons back off the crossbar before Fulham scramble clear.
Diaz cuts onto his right foot before curling goalwards, but his shot is straight down the throat of Leno, who makes an easy save.
Liverpool have started this second half brightly, though so far Fulham are surviving.
Fulham have won none of their last six away Premier League games (three draws, three defeats), though their last win was on Merseyside in August, a 1-0 win at Everton.
Indeed, Fulham have won four of their last five away league games against Everton and Liverpool, having only won one of their first 55 such visits in league football beforehand.
Diaz again fires straight at Leno, and the Colombia international will be disappointed not to have worked the goalkeeper more in this game having scored against LASK in midweek.
Nunez has hit the woodwork five times this season.
That's over twice as often as any other Premier League player (15 players have hit it two times).
CHANCE! Salah manages to nudge a deft header towards Nunez in the Fulham box, but the striker skews his shot and the ball bounces harmlessly wide of the target.
It has just not quite happened for Nunez so far in this game.
Having scored against his former team earlier, Wilson makes way for Cairney in Silva's first substitution.
Pereira has created three of Fulham's five chances, but he is now replaced by Willian.
The former Arsenal man will be looking to find the back of the net again here having done so twice in the win over Wolves.
Klopp also looks to his bench, first opting to bring on Gakpo for Szoboszlai, who did not have his best game.
Klopp also decides to bring on Gomez for Mac Allister, which surely means Alexander-Arnold will move into midfield, with the substitute slotting in at right-back.
Matip has a problem here, and Klopp may be forced into another change with the centre-back down and clutching at his knee.
Matip's game is indeed over, and he limps off for Konate.
Gravenberch opts to go for an ambitious long-range strike, but it proves to be a poor decision as his shot is straight at Leno, who makes the save.
Liverpool have produced 18 shots compared to Fulham's seven, yet their xG (expected goals) tally of 1.04 is only slightly higher than the visitors' (1).
Silva again looks to his substitutes, bringing on De Cordova-Reid for Iwobi to freshen up their attack.
Tete also makes way having levelled for Fulham in first-half added time.
Castagne is on in his place.
Reed looks a little shaken up after a challenge in midfield, though the Fulham man will try and soldier on.
Willian slides a throughball into the path of Robinson, though Kelleher gets down well to make the save before scooping up the ball to prevent any lurking Fulham attackers turning home.

GOOOAAALLL!!! FULHAM LEAD FOR THE FIRST TIME!!! Are we in for a huge shock at Anfield? Cairney dinks an inviting ball towards the back post, where De Cordova-Reid does brilliantly to leap over Tsimikas and nod into the back of the net! Klopp will be fuming with the defending, as the visitors go 3-2 up!
Cairney links up with his fellow substitute, lofting a brilliant delivery over for De Cordova-Reid to power home a header.
Having twice led, Liverpool now find themselves behind at Anfield.
This could be a huge blow to their hopes of lifting the Premier League title, and Klopp will be desperate to see a response from his team.
Klopp responds to Fulham's third goal by bringing on Endo for Gravenberch in midfield.
BIG CHANCE! Salah spurns a golden opportunity for his 200th Liverpool goal and a leveller.
Diaz nods goalwards from a corner, and Leno can only parry into the path of Salah at the back post.
The Egypt international shoots from a difficult angle, but the ball flies over the crossbar, much to Fulham's relief.
Klopp's men are starting to ramp up the pressure now as they seek a way back into this game.
Fulham could be in for a nervy last couple of minutes.
GOOOAAALLL!!! ENDO MAKES IT 3-3!!! That is exactly the type of impact Klopp will have wanted from his substitutes as Endo fires home.
Salah lays it off to the midfielder on the edge of the box, and Endo places into the top right corner, giving Leno no chance and equalising for Liverpool.
Can they go on and win this now?
Salah's layoff was perfectly weighted for Endo to fire home.

GOOOAAALLL!!! ALEXANDER-ARNOLD MAKES IT 4-3!!! REMARKABLE!!! How quickly can your fortunes change in football? Having been behind just moments ago, Liverpool now lead thanks to Alexander-Arnold's fine finish.
Gakpo sees a shot saved, but Fulham cannot clear their lines and the ball comes out to Alexander-Arnold.
The 25-year-old brings it down before rifling into the bottom left corner to spark wild celebrations at Anfield!
Tsimikas nudged the ball back for Alexander-Arnold to fire Liverpool in front.
Silva reacts to the rapid turnaround by bringing on Vinicius for Reed in an attacking change.
We are into seven minutes of additional time.
Will there still be more late drama to come? Given the way this game has gone, it would come as no surprise!
Liverpool are looking to keep the ball now as the seconds tick down on what would be a hugely satisfying victory.
Fulham are struggling to get hold of possession at the minute, and Liverpool are doing a much better job of seeing the game out than the one Fulham did.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 4-3 FULHAM
The full-time whistle blows to bring a quite remarkable game to an end, as Liverpool take the spoils with a 4-3 triumph at Anfield.

They were twice pegged back in the first half, with Alexander-Arnold's exquisite free-kick opener that went in off Leno's back cancelled out by Wilson, before Tete levelled on the stroke of half-time after Mac Allister had put Liverpool back in front with another great strike.
Fulham then got their noses in front for the first time with 10 minutes to play, De Cordova-Reid powering a header home to put the visitors on the verge of a shock away win.
Things would all go wrong for Silva's men, though, and Endo came off the bench to level before Alexander-Arnold sparked jubilant celebrations as he lashed home for the eventual winner.
That could prove to be a vital comeback victory for Liverpool, as they move to within two points of leaders Arsenal at the Premier League summit.
For Fulham, they remain just eight points above the bottom three.
They will look to bounce back when they host Nottingham Forest on Wednesday, while Liverpool will travel to take on struggling Sheffield United the same day, looking to continue their great form.
That is all we have from Anfield, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
